chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti said: Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the mukatab (a slave who has contracted for manumission in exchange for a sum), if he is contracted and pays part of his manumission money, then dies leaving a son and wealth greater than what he still owes for the manumission, it is said: 'The masters are paid the remainder of the manumission amount, and what remains is for his son.'

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a deceased mukatab distributed if he leaves surplus wealth after paying his manumission debt?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the priority of the mukatab's debt to his master over general inheritance, ensuring the manumission contract is fulfilled before any surplus passes to heirs. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the 'debt' of manumission is treated as a secured obligation against the estate, distinct from other liabilities, thereby protecting the master's right while allowing the son to inherit the remainder.
